sents.t: As assistant manager, I now get better health insurance from work.
But choosing a plan was confusing.
One plan had a low monthly premium but a high deductible.
The other had a higher premium and a lower deductible.
Danny explained it to me over coffee.
“The deductible is the amount you pay before your insurance starts paying. If you rarely go to the doctor, the cheaper plan will be fine. If you get sick often, the other plan will save you money.”
I chose the cheaper plan and made an appointment for my first full checkup in America.
Dr. Patel checked my blood pressure, listened to my heart, and asked a lot of questions.
“Do you smoke? How much do you exercise? How many hours do you sleep?”
“I’ve been training for a half marathon,” I said proudly.
“Great. Your heart is very healthy,” she said.
“But your blood test shows that your vitamin D is low. If you take a vitamin every day, you’ll feel more energetic, especially in winter.”
At the front desk, I paid a twenty-dollar copay.
The checkup was free with my plan, but the blood test wasn’t.
“If you have any questions about your results, call us,” the receptionist said.
